name: pair_discount_arb
author: BlitzkriegBot
description: Pair-discount collector for binary rounds (@almach mechanism): when ask_UP + ask_DOWN + entry fees < max_pair_cost, buy BOTH legs with EQUAL declared share counts and collect by merging the complete pairs into $1.00/pair of collateral. Profit is locked at entry; the exit is a collection, not a decision — the kernel intercepts the strategy's merge intents before the sell ladder. Entries are pure maker (entry_maker) and v1.3 quotes them where a post-only buy can actually REST: entry_quote_mode 1 (default) = ask − entry_reprice_ticks (0.01 grid), 2 = mid floored to the grid, 3 = the bid, 0 = v1.2's at-ask — the kernel refuses an at-ask post-only POST (#464 WouldCross), which is why v1.2 filled 0/N (10/15 replay: 4 orders, 4 venue.WouldCross). The @almach corpus confirms the path: maker prints land 1–3 ticks below the then-ask, taker prints at it, never above. The discount test stays on the asks (a fill only prints cheaper); a leg with no restable quote skips the attempt (fail closed). Gap-fill top-ups quote by the same policy (an at-ask top-up is refused exactly like an at-ask entry), their incremental test unchanged (ask+fee vs max_top_up_cost). v1.2's entry_window 0.5 (NEW pair attempts confined to the round's first half) is unchanged. Fees priced from bk.fees(); no schedule in force means no entries. Signal-only: the kernel adjudicates, sizes, gates, merges and settles every intent.
